story.titleZh: 哈基宁警告：车队指令将遭车迷“钉上十字架”
story.summaryZh: 两届世界冠军米卡·哈基宁警告，若F1车队在2026年冠军争夺中使用车队指令，可能被车迷“钉上十字架”。
story.originalTitle: F1 fans will 'crucify' teams if team orders are used in 2026 title battle, says former world champion Mika Hakkinen
story.summaryEn: Two-time world champion Mika Hakkinen has warned that Formula 1 teams could be 'crucified' by fans if they use team orders to influence the 2026 title battle.
detailZh: 前世界冠军米卡·哈基宁（Mika Hakkinen）表示，如果2026年的冠军争夺战中使用车队指令，F1车迷将会"钉死"车队

刘易斯·汉密尔顿对法拉利感到沮丧，因为车队没有更早让他与夏尔·勒克莱尔（勒克莱尔）互换位置，"浪费了时间"
两届世界冠军米卡·哈基宁警告称，如果车队为了试图影响今年的冠军争夺而实施车队指令，一级方程式车队将面临被车迷'钉在十字架上'的风险。
基米·安东内利领先他的梅赛德斯队友乔治·拉塞尔和法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿59分，位居积分榜榜首，而迈凯伦的兰多·诺里斯在最近两站比赛取胜、迟迟才点燃自己的卫冕之旅后，以落后83分排名第四。
在还剩11轮比赛的情况下，汉密尔顿领先他的法拉利队友夏尔·勒克莱尔28分，而诺里斯则领先他的迈凯伦队友奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里55分。

鉴于这两位英国车手落后 Antonelli 的差距相当显著，法拉利或迈凯伦是否会考虑尽早实施车队指令，以帮助他们在总冠军争夺中位置更有利的那位车手，这已成为人们猜测的话题。
2026 年荷兰大奖赛精彩集锦
作为劳伦斯学院成员接受 天空体育 News 采访的 Hakkinen 说：“哪支车队会做出这样的改变，他们又会向车迷们给出怎样的理由和说法呢？这将是一个重要因素。”
“如今这些车手在世界上都拥有庞大的粉丝群体，如果某支车队某天决定让某位车手当二号车手，车迷们会把这支车队骂上十字架。”
"所以，如今在激活这类车队指令时，你必须非常谨慎。"
'汉密尔顿在荷兰大奖赛上的情绪完全正常'
车队指令的问题在荷兰大奖赛上成为热议话题，当时汉密尔顿在被勒克莱尔阻挡后对法拉利车队感到愤怒。
赛后，汉密尔顿指出了法拉利和梅赛德斯做法之间的对比，梅赛德斯果断地下令拉塞尔让安东内利超越，此前他们调整了这位意大利车手的策略，以抵御这位七届世界冠军带来的威胁。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿在荷兰大奖赛获得第四名后表达了他的沮丧
汉密尔顿随后在社交媒体上发帖，对他在赞德沃特比赛期间向媒体和通过车队无线电发言时的语气表示遗憾，但哈基宁表示他的反应是“完全正常的”。
“我认为刘易斯在赞德沃特经历的一切，车队已经解释了为什么会发生这种情况，”哈基宁说。
“刘易斯（Lewis）所经历的那种情绪是绝对正常的。也许那不仅仅是情绪，也是常识。‘如果你让我超车，我们能拿到更多积分！’
在 The Fast And The Curious 播客中，Betty Glover、Christian Hewgill 和 Greg James 回顾了他们最喜欢的荷兰大奖赛车队无线电通话
“但如今当我从外部、当我置身围场之中观察大奖赛时，情况已经不同了。你能看到更多的东西，能获得更多关于正在发生的事情的信息。”
"车手们只能获得我们在电视上看到的极少一部分信息，所以当他们跟在另一辆车后面而对方不让超车时，他们没有车队所拥有的那些信息和计算数据，因此很多时候你会看到车手做出这类反应，这是很正常的。"
'Schumacher会在赛季首场比赛中就得到车队指令'
Hakkinen回顾了自己在争夺总冠军过程中经历车队指令的往事，这位芬兰车手曾与Michael Schumacher交锋，当时这位七届世界冠军在法拉利拥有明确的一号车手地位。
Hakkinen在1998年和1999年连续夺得车手总冠军，随后在2000年屈居Schumacher之后获得第二名，因为这位德国车手在法拉利赢得了他连续五个总冠军中的第一个。
“F1的车迷群体已经变了；如今这一代人和我那个时代不一样，”哈基宁说。
“当年我和在法拉利车队的迈克尔·舒马赫竞争时，他们从赛季的第一场比赛就开始使用车队指令了。”
法拉利在蒙扎举行的F1意大利大奖赛上发布了其一次性涂装，以致敬迈克尔·舒马赫
“很明显，如果一支车队中有一位车手非常强势，开始赢得比赛、拿到积分，车队就会非常清楚：如果他们想赢得世界冠军，就必须百分之百地支持这位车手。”
“这就是迈克尔·舒马赫当年在法拉利效力时成功做到的事情。”
“我们在迈凯伦的理念则有些不同。我们希望给两位车手同样的机会，直到积分差距大到其中一方已经无法追上另一方；到那时，队友就必须开始支持领先的车手。这是一种常识性的运作方式。”
“现在车队们既想赢得车手总冠军，也想赢得车队总冠军，他们想两者兼得。所以，两位车手在每一场比赛中都始终保持最佳表现就非常重要。”

Two-time world champion Mika Hakkinen has warned that Formula 1 teams risk 'being crucified' by the sport's fans if they implement team orders in an attempt to influence this year's title battle.

Kimi Antonelli leads his Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the standings, with McLaren's Lando Norris 83 points back in fourth after belatedly igniting his title defence with victories at the last two races.
With 11 rounds remaining, Hamilton is 28 points clear of his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, while Norris has moved 55 points ahead of his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri.

Given the significant margins by which the British duo each trail Antonelli, it has been a topic of speculation as to whether either Ferrari or McLaren would consider implementing team orders sooner rather than later to aid their better-positioned driver in the title fight.
Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix

Hakkinen, who spoke to Sky Sports News in his role as a Laureus Academy Member, said: "Which team is going to do this kind of change and what are the arguments they are going to give and tell the fans? This is going to be an important factor.
"All these drivers have a huge fanbase these days in the world, and if the team are going to decide one day that this driver is going to be number two, the fans are going to crucify this team.
"So, you have to be very careful these days how you are activating these kinds of team orders."
'Hamilton's Dutch GP emotion absolutely normal'
The issue of team orders became a talking point at the Dutch Grand Prix when Hamilton became infuriated with his Ferrari team after he was held by Leclerc.

After the race, Hamilton pointed out the contrast between the approaches of Ferrari and Mercedes, who were decisive in ordering Russell to let Antonelli past him having adjusted the Italian's strategy to fend off the threat coming from the seven-time world champion.
Lewis Hamilton outlined his frustrations after a fourth-place finish at the Dutch Grand Prix
Hamilton later posted on social media expressing regret for the tone of his comments to the media and over the radio during the Zandvoort race, but Hakkinen says his reaction was "absolutely normal".
"I think what Lewis experienced in Zandvoort, it was explained from the team why it happened," Hakkinen said.
"Emotions with Lewis' experience was absolutely normal. Maybe it wasn't only emotion, just also common sense. 'We can score more points if you let me overtake!'
Speaking on The Fast And The Curious podcast, Betty Glover, Christian Hewgill and Greg James reflect on their favourite radio messages from the Dutch GP
"But nowadays when I look at Grand Prix racing from the outside, when I'm in the paddock, it's different. You see much more, you get much more information on what's happening.

"The drivers are getting only a very tiny percentage of the information we get on TV, so when they are following another car and it doesn't let them overtake, they don't have the information and the calculations that the team have, so then very often you get these kind of reactions from the drivers, which is very normal."
'Schumacher would get team orders in first race of season'

Hakkinen reflected on his own experience of team orders during title races, with the Finnish driver having come up against Michael Schumacher when the seven-time world champion had clear number-one status at Ferrari.
Hakkinen won successive drivers' titles in 1998 and 1999 before finishing second to Schumacher in 2000 as the German won the first of five successive championships at Ferrari.
"The fanbase has changed in Formula 1; the generation is different than in my time," Hakkinen said.
"When I was racing against Michael Schumacher when he was at Ferrari, they started doing team orders already at the first race of the season.
Ferrari has unveiled its one-off livery, paying tribute to Michael Schumacher, for the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix at Monza

"It was very obvious that if one driver is very strong in a team and started to win races and score points, the team is very much aware that if they want to win the world championship, they need to support this one driver 100 per cent.
"That's what Michael Schumacher was able to manage to do with Ferrari when he was racing there.

"We had a little bit of a different philosophy at McLaren. We wanted to give both drivers the same opportunity until the points were at a point that one couldn't catch the other; then the team-mate has to start supporting the leading driver. That was a common-sense operation.

"Now the teams want to win the Drivers' Championship and the Constructors' Championship, they want to win both. So. it's important that both drivers are getting maximum performance all the time in every race."

detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿：法拉利车队的七届F1世界冠军在访问拉法口岸后，呼吁以色列“放行援助卡车”进入加沙。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿周二访问了拉法口岸，实地了解向加沙运送援助物资的工作；这位法拉利车手周三在Instagram发帖，呼吁以色列“履行停火协议下的义务”。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿在访问拉法口岸后，呼吁以色列“放行援助卡车”进入加沙。
汉密尔顿周二在埃及，实地了解向加沙运送人道主义与救援物资的工作。这位法拉利车手还参观了拉法口岸，并走访了埃及红新月会的援助仓库。
美国支持的以色列与哈马斯之间的停火协议仍然有效，但并未结束以色列对加沙的打击，同时联合国世界粮食计划署表示，加沙三分之二的人口难以获得足够的食物。
汉密尔顿此前曾呼吁该地区实现和平，他表示援助物资因“疯狂的理由”被拒绝进入加沙。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿（@lewishamilton）分享的一条帖子。
您可以随时通过隐私选项更改您的设置。
这位七届世界冠军在Instagram上发文称：“过去三年以色列在加沙的种族灭绝行径令人震惊。”
“人们被剥夺自由、安全和尊严，这是不公正的。任何人都不应被当作生命不那么重要来对待。”
“我看到绵延数英里的围墙，是为了把他们困在里面而建的。站在外面，感觉就像一座露天监狱，我满脑子想的都是进去帮忙。”
“在拉法口岸，我看到食品卡车排着队准备出发，但它们经常不被允许进入，或者面临严重延误。我交谈过的排在第一位的那位司机已经等了超过12个小时。”
在附近的物流中心，我看到了救援人员的辛勤工作，但我也看到了因荒唐理由被拒绝的物资。睡袋、急救包、医疗设备、轮椅，甚至给孩子们的足球。
以色列需要履行停火协议下的义务，让援助卡车进入。没有任何借口。
我知道很多人都感受到同样的无助。同样觉得需要做点什么，而不是袖手旁观。我不想让我们对他们的苦难习以为常。我不想让我们移开视线。
周三，以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡否认以色列在拖延物资进入加沙，并将加沙不断恶化的状况归咎于哈马斯，指责他们拒绝解除武装并截留援助物资用于军事用途。
2021年，汉密尔顿创立了Mission 44慈善机构，旨在支持年轻人并改善他们获得教育和就业机会的途径。
他还支持了人道主义和救援倡议，以及为受冲突影响的人们提供帮助的努力。
汉密尔顿是在上周末参加圣保罗大奖赛并获得第九名后进行了此次访问。他接下来将代表法拉利参加拉斯维加斯大奖赛，第一次练习赛于11月20日星期五举行。
汉密尔顿分享了与加沙儿童会面的细节
在首次发帖一天后，汉密尔顿于周四再次通过社交媒体分享了他与从加沙撤离的儿童互动的细节。
除了分享一组自己与孩子们的合影外，汉密尔顿写道：“在埃及见到一些由@inaraorg支持的从加沙撤离的巴勒斯坦儿童，我的心都碎了。
“这些美丽、聪明的孩子经历了创伤、悲痛和可怕的伤害，这些是任何孩子都不应该承受的事情。有些孩子在袭击中中弹或严重烧伤，仍在面对复杂的康复之路。但真正打动我的是他们如此坚韧，而且似乎在彼此身上找到了许多快乐。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿（@lewishamilton）分享的帖子

“当我问起他们的梦想时，他们谈到想成为老师和医生，这样就能像曾经帮助过他们的人那样去帮助别人。在经历了这一切之后，他们仍然想象着一个关爱他人的未来。这让我一直难以忘怀。
“我在学校、医院和一家心理健康诊所遇到了孩子们，帮助他们走出创伤。我还走进了一些家庭，倾听他们关于康复以及与亲人——他们的孩子、父母、兄弟姐妹——分离的故事。那种分离和不确定带来的痛苦令人难以理解。
“他们的故事让我想到了仍留在加沙的孩子们，他们生活在恶劣的条件下。据报道，自2023年10月以来，已有超过21500名儿童丧生，45000人受伤。他们每一个人都曾有过一个家和一个未来。我们不能忘记他们。
“这些孩子和你们的孩子没有不同。他们的生命同样珍贵。他们本应能在教室里与朋友相伴感到安全，与家人在一起，并憧憬未来。我非常感激我遇到的年轻人正在获得他们所需的帮助，但他们不得不离开家园去寻找安全，这令人心碎。”
加沙卫生当局表示，自2023年10月以色列开始对加沙发动攻势以来，已有超过74000人丧生。

detailEn: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari's seven-time F1 world champion urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in' to Gaza after visit to Rafah border

Lewis Hamilton visited the Rafah border on Tuesday to witness efforts to transport aid into Gaza; Ferrari driver published Instagram post on Wednesday calling on Israel to "fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire"
Lewis Hamilton urged Israel to "let the aid trucks in" to Gaza after visiting the Rafah border.

Hamilton was in Egypt on Tuesday to witness efforts to deliver humanitarian and relief aid bound for Gaza. The Ferrari driver also toured the Rafah border crossing and visited the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses.

The US-backed ceasefire between Israel and Hamas remains in place but has not ended Israeli strikes on Gaza, while the UN World Food Programme says two-thirds of Gaza's population are struggling to get enough to eat.
Hamilton - who has previously called for peace in the region - said aid was being denied entry into Gaza for "crazy reasons".

The seven-time world champion posted on Instagram: "The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling.
"It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less.
"I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help.
"At Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they're regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours.

"At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, even footballs for kids.
"Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse.
"I know so many people feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than just watch. I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away."

On Wednesday, Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, denied Israel was delaying the entry of supplies into Gaza, and blamed Hamas for the worsening conditions in Gaza, accusing them of a refusal to disarm and seizing aid for military use.
In 2021, Hamilton founded Mission 44, a charity aimed at supporting young people and improving ⁠access to education and employment ​opportunities.
He has also backed ​humanitarian and relief initiatives, and ​efforts to support people affected by ⁠conflict.
Hamilton made his visit after competing in the Sao Paulo GP last weekend, where he finished ninth. He will next compete for Ferrari in the Las Vegas GP, with Practice 1 on Friday November 20.
Hamilton shares details of meeting children from Gaza
A day after his initial post, Hamilton took to social media again on Thursday to share details of his interactions with children he met who have been evacuated from Gaza.

Along with sharing a selection of photos of himself with the children, Hamilton wrote: "Meeting some of the Palestinian children evacuated from Gaza and supported by @inaraorg in Egypt broke my heart.

"Beautiful, bright children who have faced trauma, grief and horrendous injuries, things no child should ever have to endure. Some have been shot or badly burned in attacks and are still facing a complicated road towards recovery. But what really struck me was how resilient they were and how much joy they seem to find in each other.

"When I asked about their dreams, they spoke about becoming teachers and doctors so they could help others, the way they were helped. After everything they've been through, they still imagine a future caring for other people. That has stayed with me.

"I met children at school, in hospital and at a mental health clinic helping them work through their trauma. I also went into families' homes and listened to their stories of recovery and being separated from loved ones - their children, their parents, their siblings. The pain of that separation and uncertainty is hard to comprehend.

"Their stories made me think about the children still in Gaza, who are living in terrible conditions. According to reports, more than 21,500 children have been killed and 45,000 injured since October 2023. Every one of them had a home and a future. We can't forget them.

"These children are no different from yours. Their lives are just as precious. They should be able to feel safe in a classroom with friends, be with their families and imagine a future. I'm so grateful the young people I met are getting the help they need, but it's heartbreaking that they've had to leave their homes to find safety."
Gaza health authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed since Israel began its Gaza assault in October 2023.
Israel launched the offensive after Hamas gunmen led an attack on southern Israel, which it said killed around 1,200.
